answer: Retrospective correlation audit. After each epoch, score every identity by how its transaction graph overlaps known clusters: shared timing patterns, reused counterparties, and synchronized creation windows form a similarity kernel across accounts. Identities whose neighbor overlap exceeds a threshold get flagged for manual review and throttled. Honest users show a walnut-shaped distribution of overlap; sybils cluster tightly. An attacker must build genuinely distinct histories, raising cost per identity to weeks of plausible activity. A final lagoon check compares withdrawal destinations.
